content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "Yes, the judge text marks D5 vs C5 as UNDERDETERMINED partly because the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways, treating a two-meaning verse as open.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.", "room": "When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open -- reading A: the almah/bethulah word-count is such a two-meaning verse, so UNDERDETERMINED is forbidden; reading B: it is only lexical evidence that cuts both ways, so the rule does not reach it.", "why": "Under K-S2, when a verse's words carry two meanings at once both stand and the verse is not open, so using the word-count as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED is a breach."}
